focus_group.description: According to the European project PANORAIMA (Pan-European Network for Responsible Artificial Intelligence Multisector Masters’ Programme/GA101189994, the University of West Attica conducted one (1) focus group to identify the pedagogical needs of the project, in line with WP2/T2.2 requirements. More specifically, according to the GA, partner universities should determine internal requirements concerning pedagogics, course delivery, and programme restrictions related to the delivery of the PANORAIMA, utilising focus groups. Consequently, a focus group discussion took place on July 4, 2025, from 12:00 to 14:00 (CET) exploring the pedagogical and organisational needs relevant to the project's development. The research was approved by the Research Ethics Committee of the University of West Attica (Ref. No. 54225 - 16/06/2025) and conducted online via Microsoft Teams.
focus_group.aim: The main target of the focus group was to engage leaders and key actors from Universities and Research Academia, to understand, record and organise pedagogical needs for the implementation of Human-Centric education in Artificial Intelligence.

findings.title: Hybrid preferred, blended requested
findings.quote: Most tutors prefer to teach through a hybrid format (on-site teaching + online teaching, simultaneously). However, through the discussion, the need for a blended learning model (on-site lectures + online lectures, at separate times) emerged.

findings.title: Project-based beats lectures
findings.quote: Project/Problem/Self-paced and personalised learning is preferred instead of traditional instructional lectures. The former entails the adoption of corresponding learning strategies i.e. flipped classroom, on-the-job training.

findings.title: AI in the classroom — but with sustainability concerns
findings.quote: The adoption of AI in education dictates more AI-assisted frameworks, AI tools in the classroom, recognising the profound impact of Artificial Intelligence on education.

findings.title: Smartphones > manuscripts
findings.quote: Digital tools, especially smartphones, laptops, and corresponding software (i.e. mobile apps, online tools), remain more preferable than hardcopy manuscripts for student engagement or learning. Robots and chatbots follow.

findings.title: AI-reliance is the new cognitive risk
findings.quote: Most participants highlighted AI Reliance as a high risk, since students rely too much on AI for quick and easy responses.

findings.title: Collaborative over individual
findings.quote: Most participants agreed that the current pedagogical needs require more collaborative learning strategies, with self-paced learning being the second most popular response.

findings.title: The classroom agreement
findings.quote: A classroom agreement could help in that direction, as teachers and students could sign a classroom agreement, in which the rules for using AI with Responsibility, Transparency and oversight are established.

questions.text: How do tutors mostly teach today? What teaching methods do they prefer?
questions.summary: Hybrid (on-site + online simultaneously) was most common, but the group pushed toward a true blended model (on-site + online at separate times).

questions.text: How should teachers adapt their teaching methods in the next 5 years, given the rise of AI in education?
questions.summary: Shift toward AI-assisted frameworks and in-class AI tools, with an equivalent emphasis on sustainability and responsible-AI practice.

questions.text: How much time do students spend studying per day today?
questions.summary: Study-time patterns vary widely across partner universities; framed as context for the learning-strategy discussion.

questions.text: Which media or tools do you find most effective for student engagement or learning? (manuscripts, digital tools, mobile apps, etc.)
questions.summary: Smartphones, laptops, and supporting software dominated; robots and chatbots followed; hardcopy manuscripts came last.

questions.text: Do students face issues or threats regarding critical or creative thinking? Do they need to use less or more technology?
questions.summary: Over-reliance on AI for quick answers was flagged as the highest risk to critical and creative thinking.

questions.text: In your opinion, what are our students' pedagogical needs now or in the next 5 years?
questions.summary: Collaborative learning strategies first; self-paced learning second.

questions.text: What kind of guidance do students need from teachers to use AI tools effectively and responsibly?
questions.summary: Understand how models are trained (explainability); show prompts (transparency); know good/bad practice; use AI as assistant not guide.

questions.text: What specific sectoral or societal challenges related to AI (ethical governance, regulatory compliance, public trust) should syllabi address?
questions.summary: Ethical governance, regulatory compliance, risk assessment, and sustainability top the list — followed by transparency, interdisciplinarity, explainability, misinformation.

questions.text: What types of AI-related skills, knowledge or professional roles are most necessary to support responsible AI across all sectors?
questions.summary: A ranked list of 14 skills — explainability, ethics, and critical thinking lead; see the skills ranking section.

questions.text: Do you include ethical dilemmas and legal issues in your assessments? If yes, what is your approach?
questions.summary: Real case studies from industry / public sector for analysing bias and fairness; AI-generated work heavily penalised; scepticism about LLM use during online assessments.

questions.text: How should teachers embed ethical and legal issues in real-world AI scenarios?
questions.summary: Encourage critical thinking, discussion, and responsible decision-making using real AI use-cases in assignments.

questions.text: Any additional points about human-centric AI in the EU or how PANORAIMA can strengthen the AI ecosystem?
questions.summary: Myth-busting for public communication; stronger technical-social interdisciplinarity; ethically-driven, inclusive (incl. older learners) syllabi; more free/open educational resources; sustainability in AI curricula.
